previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of AML in remission following stem cell transplant and chronic extensive sclerodermic skin GVHD was admitted for shortness of breath and dry cough. Imaging revealed bilateral lower lobe ground-glass opacities concerning for pneumonia, and he was treated with cefepime and azithromycin. Blood and respiratory cultures were negative, and fungal markers were non-diagnostic. His respiratory status improved, oxygen was weaned, and antibiotics were completed. He developed persistent cough, and CT sinuses showed chronic sinusitis with purulent drainage; cultures were negative, and he was managed with nasal irrigation and topical therapies. IL-2 for GVHD was held initially but restarted. He was discharged home with improved symptoms and instructions for ongoing sinus care and medication adjustments.

#Chronic ___ wounds: Pt reports increasing pain and extent of 
wounds. Wound care nurse at ___ ___ for worsening exudate 
and foul smell. He is immunosuppresed with skin breakdown from 
chronic GVHD possibly infected ulcers with polymicrobial wound 
culture growing pseudomonas and MSSA; however, per ID it is 
suspect if this is causing infection vs colonization. Past micro 
also shows polymicrobial infections with pseudomonas and MSSA 
and the ___ did not look frankly cellulitic. Per ID, 
drainage and foul smell are not the best indicators of 
infection; however, the increased pain he experienced, was, ___ 
their mind's a reason to treat with IV Zosyn for 7 days with 
much improvement ___ pain, smell, and discharge. Per Derm, GVHD 
alone can cause ulcers and optimizing his GVHD medications may 
be more helpful and derm suggested topical Tacro if not 
prohibited on his IL-2 trial. His MRSA screen was negative. Derm 
also recommended topical flagyl alternating with topical 
gentamiacin every two weeks. They also added a Dakin's solution 
to his wound care regimen.   

# Diarrhea - had several episodes daily that were more than his 
typical GVHD stools. C. diff was negative and we felt it was 
most likely Abx-associated as he is on Zosyn. He became 
dehydrated with bump ___ Cr to 1.4 and fluids were given with
